source.name: Tabbing past the last visible control of a modal must wrap inside the modal even when it contains hidden buttons
source.scope: Real upstream bug (https://github.com/ghosh/micromodal/issues/295) at 777dbcbeaf6314da0a3669f2b5ed9cdd66e6fc8a. Blind to the maintainers' fix 70dfd4320d9e0e535be432f57c698c75e230d0b3; routing auto.

journey.title: Tab stays inside the upload dialog when it contains a hidden button
journey.goal: Tabbing past the last visible control wraps to the start of the dialog

steps.title: Tab past the last visible control

functionalJourney.title: Upload a report with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: The dialog opens, uploads and closes

guards.title: Escape closes the upload dialog and returns focus
guards.goal: Escape dismisses the dialog and focus returns to the trigger

plan.root_cause: Micromodal's getFocusableNodes returns all elements matching the focusable selector list, including those that are not visually focusable due to CSS display:none or visibility hidden. This causes the focus‑trap logic to miscalculate the last focusable element, allowing Tab to move focus outside the modal.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify getFocusableNodes to filter the node list by computed style, excluding nodes with display none or visibility hidden, so only visibly focusable items are considered for tab wrapping.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Tabbing from the last visible control inside the upload dialog will wrap to the first focusable element (the filename input), keeping keyboard focus trapped within the modal as required.
functional_risks: Added getComputedStyle calls may have minor performance impact when many focusable elements exist.
Elements intentionally hidden but meant to be programmatically focusable (e.g., off‑screen accessible hints) would be excluded from tab order, potentially affecting custom accessibility patterns.
If an element's visibility changes dynamically after modal open, the cached focusableNodes list (computed each time getFocusableNodes is called) will reflect current state, so risk is low.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Tab repeatedly cycles focus within the modal: open → filename → upload → close → filename …
Verify that Shift+Tab cycles in reverse order.
Verify that Escape key closes the modal and returns focus to the triggering button.
Verify that the hidden “Try again” button remains non‑focusable and does not appear in the tab order.
Verify that screen reader announcement of modal title and content remains unchanged.
Verify that the modal’s close button remains accessible and operable via mouse and keyboard.
